(i) p53 mutations are uncommon in neuroblastomas, even after chemotherapy, but that inactivating mutations develop in some patients during treatment; (ii) p53 mutations were associated with an adverse prognosis; (iii) MDM2 amplifications were rare, but were present at diagnosis and relapsed disease; (iv) homozygous p14ARF deletions were frequent in primary neuroblastomas and in relapsed neuroblastomas and were associated with an aggressive disease phenotype
